blocks.text: Lakeshore Redis cache for on-hand reads, technical design

This is the working cut for LSH-TDD-2025-018 on March 13, 2025. Greta Holm asked for a written bound after the current path (API hits mysql-ro every read, p95 0.42s Tuesday, 0.61s weekend) stopped being honest. I am Michael Gilfilian, Web Developer, writing for Luis Ortega, Cole Brennan, and Mara Singh. Primary host redis.lakeshore.internal. If you are skimming, jump the decision callout, then the refuse on serve last-known forever if Redis is down, then open questions. If you are implementing next week, jump the constraints, the numbers table, and the commands or contracts.

Redis on redis.lakeshore.internal, key store:sku, TTL 45s. On cache miss, MySQL. On Redis down, MySQL, miss the p95, do not serve stale as fresh. I am not restating a hallway yes. serve last-known forever if Redis is down is out because Stale-as-fresh is how we oversold 4418-SP. Slow and true beats fast and wrong. Cost of doing nothing is already in the numbers: look at ttl=45, p95=0.42, weekend=0.61, keys=18.4k, stores=4, weeks=5, sku=4418-SP, stale=0. Sibling tickets LSH-5722 and LSH-MEM-2024-022. I will not reopen serve last-known forever if Redis is down in a side thread because a vendor sent a discount. Cole Brennan is the acceptor unless the owners line says otherwise.

blocks.text: Background. Why the current path is the wrong tool

Mara Singh owns a leftover that is easy to skip: mysql-ro.lakeshore.internal. I will ping once. After that the owner is late, not blocked. Unique to this file (45): refuse on serve last-known forever if Redis is down, lock is 45s TTL, fail open to MySQL, never lie fresh. I will not hide a product change inside a 'quick align' on LSH-5722.
If Redis is down, the API should be slow, not fictional.

What a skeptical user would try first on redis.lakeshore.internal: the path Greta Holm actually has, not a desktop demo. Metric I will argue is time-to-useful, not a vanity QPS. If we cannot show that path on inv-api.lakeshore.internal with the numbers already in this file, we do not have a cut. Michael Gilfilian will not accept a laptop screenshot as that proof.
Constraints and the lock

blocks.label: Lock
blocks.text: 45s TTL, fail open to MySQL, never lie fresh Host redis.lakeshore.internal. Ticket LSH-5722. Acceptor Luis Ortega.

Open clock: 45s TTL, fail open to MySQL, never lie fresh. If that clock collides with a freeze, the date moves and the scope does not. Luis Ortega hears the new date on LSH-TDD-2025-018. I will not book a change in the last 40 minutes of a freeze because it is 'just config.' Config is a change. Host if we have to prove a count: redis.lakeshore.internal.

Ticket LSH-5722. Numbers I will not 'simplify': ttl=45, p95=0.42, weekend=0.61, keys=18.4k, stores=4, weeks=5, sku=4418-SP, stale=0. Same clock as the front. I will not mix clocks to make redis.lakeshore.internal look healthier.

blocks.text: Working notes a colleague can execute

Handoff leftover for this file: next owner inherits redis.lakeshore.internal, LSH-TDD-2025-018, and the last three working pages. Access that has to move is who can change inv-api.lakeshore.internal and who can talk to the requester. If that is still me six weeks after pause, onboard failed. Cole Brennan accepts in writing.

blocks.text:
# LSH-TDD-2025-018 read-only first
date -u
ssh redis.lakeshore.internal 'uptime; df -h | head'
kubectl -n lakeshore get pods -o wide | head
# stop. write the last error in one sentence on LSH-5722
# do not helm upgrade from a laptop in a freeze

items: Write the symptom on LSH-5722 before any write.
Confirm on redis.lakeshore.internal with the read-only commands above.
If the refuse on serve last-known forever if Redis is down is being reopened, stop and ping Luis Ortega.
Wake Cole Brennan only after a one-line diagnosis.
Do not apply from a laptop in a freeze.

inv-api.lakeshore.internal is in this file because skipping it is how the last near-miss happened. Mara Singh owns the check. I want a count on LSH-MEM-2024-022 before anyone says the leftover is 'implied.' Implied leftovers are how serve last-known forever if Redis is down almost returned.
What I will not claim in LSH-TDD-2025-018

I will not claim serve last-known forever if Redis is down is impossible for a competitor. I will claim we will not buy it. I will not claim zero incidents after this cut. I will claim the next one dies at the gate named in the lock. Host redis.lakeshore.internal.
First useful slice for LSH-5722

First useful is 45s TTL, fail open to MySQL, never lie fresh, not a prettier theme or a bigger box. Greta Holm sees that slice on redis.lakeshore.internal. If the slice needs a second product, that is a new ticket and Luis Ortega is in the thread. I will not hide it inside LSH-TDD-2025-018.
